newsitem.title: PERU: Red Cross takes stretcher into Peru siege site.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross takes stretcher into Peru siege site.

text.p: Red Cross officials took a stretcher into the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima on Wednesday, sparking speculation of an imminent release of a hostage.
The last two hostages freed by the rebels were released for health reasons.
Concern has risen in recent days for the health of the 72 VIP hostages held by roughly 15 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels since the Dec. 17 takeover.
But Red Cross spokeswoman Cecilia Baux told Reuters she was not aware of any imminent release and the stretcher would probably be used inside the residence.

"In coordination with the health ministry, it was decided to improve the conditions within the residence for the medical attention to the hostages," she said. "I don't know the details, but I think it (the stretcher) is part of that."
Nearly all the hostages are now taking medication for a variety of conditions, according to the Red Cross.
